whatLanded.mechanism: The geometry is PARSED from the vendored canonical SVG at module load. There is no hand-entered geometry constant left in report-chrome.ts, so there is no second copy of the numbers to drift.
whatLanded.driftControl: Three artifacts must agree or the suite fails: the vendored .svg on disk, its sha256 in PROVENANCE.json, and the SVG text inlined in smart-site-brand.ts. Editing any one alone is loud.
whatLanded.cloneSurvival: .gitattributes pins the assets to eol=lf. core.autocrlf=true is set in this repo and would otherwise rewrite them on checkout, breaking the sha256 on every Windows clone. Verified: the staged blob sha256 equals the recorded sha256, and git emitted no CRLF warning for the .svg paths while warning on every other new text file in the same `git add`.

threeQuestionGate.whatTriggers: .github/workflows/ci.yml on push to main, pull_request to main, and workflow_dispatch. The suite is NOT dormant: the job 'typecheck + test' ran on this PR head and reported conclusion=success.
threeQuestionGate.whatFails: A non-zero vitest exit fails the CI job and blocks the merge. Demonstrated by violation below, not assumed.
threeQuestionGate.whatBypasses: HONEST ANSWER, NOT 'none'. (1) Nothing gates hauska-map: if the owning repo changes its logo, this lock pins the OLD asset and stays green. The lock detects local tampering, never upstream movement; refreshing is a deliberate human act via PROVENANCE.json's refresh procedure. (2) The sha256 lock is bypassed by editing the asset, the hash and the inlined string together, which is indistinguishable from a legitimate refresh - by design, since that IS the refresh. (3) Anything not routed through CI. (4) The masthead assertions are relative to the parsed asset, so a corrupted asset would keep them green; that case is covered by the sha256 lock, not by them. The pair is the control, neither half alone.

ci.readBy: gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/commits/<sha>/check-runs, conclusion read as a STRING per check run, never `gh pr checks` and never an exit code
ci.failureCause: packages/retrieval typechecks engine-core's sources under a STRICTER tsconfig (noUncheckedIndexedAccess). `tsc --noEmit` inside packages/engine-core passed, so it was invisible locally. The repo-wide `pnpm typecheck` is the authoritative instrument, not the package's.
ci.fix: An at() helper that THROWS on a missing index, rather than a `!` assertion. A non-null assertion would have asserted away exactly the case the parser exists to catch.
